english.title: Destroy / damage / interfere with air navigation facilities - Aviation Security Act 1982
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) unlawfully and intentionally destroyed, damaged or interfered with property used for the provision of air navigation facilities, namely **(..SPECIFY THE AIR NAVIGATION FACILITIES..), where the destruction, damage or interference was likely to endanger the safety of aircraft in flight
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3(1) and (7) of the Aviation Security Act 1982.

english.notes:
(i) Section 3(2) of the Aviation Security Act 1982 provides that the offence applies to property used for the provision of air navigation facilities, including land, building or ship so used, and including any apparatus or equipment so used, whether it is on board an aircraft or elsewhere.
(ii) Section 3(5) of the Act provides that the offence does only apply to acts committed in the United Kingdom and to acts committed outside the United Kingdom if the offender is a United Kingdom national or if the act concerns certain civil aircraft.
(iii) Section 3(6) of the Act provides further exceptions for acts committed outside the United Kingdom if the person who commits them is not a United Kingdom national.
(iv) Section 3(8) of the Act provides that civil aircraft means any aircraft other than an aircraft used in military, customs or police service.
(v) Section 2(6) of the Act provides the meaning of unlawfully.
(vi) Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property.

other.powersofarrest:
Arrest without warrant
Section 7(1) of the Aviation Security Act 1982 provides a power of arrest without warrant where a person on an aircraft or about to embark an aircraft intends to commit this offence.
other.penalty:
INDICTMENT: Life imprisonment.
